collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: On an early walk to the stream, a villager greets neighbors of every shape and shade on a perfectly ordinary morning.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: (name1) is walking to the stream early, and the village is waking up around (him/her). An elder is out on a walking frame, already halfway to the gardens and complaining about the slope. A woman with a cloud of white hair and a wide-brimmed hat is talking to a man with no hair at all about whether it'll rain. Two deaf fishers are arguing with their hands about a net, and the argument looks very rude. A child on crutches races a child without, and loses, and demands a rematch. Somebody tall ducks under a low branch without looking. Somebody short is lifting a load that would flatten most people. There are faces of every shape and skin of every shade, and everybody is just getting on with the morning. (name1) fills (his/her) water jar and says hello to all of them, and it's a perfectly ordinary day.
